    Interviewer asks

    Platform Scope
    Requirements
    Functional: platform capabilities
    Platform
    Host AgentsWhy? A central platform controls agent workflows and the SDLC, and monitors agent execution.
    AI GatewayWhy? One entry point routes all model and MCP calls, so the casino controls cost, keys, and access.
    Retrieval Corporate KnowledgeWhy? Agents answer from approved company documents, so employees get correct and current answers.
    Security
    Define high-value targetsWhy? The casino protects first the data and tools with the highest business risk.
    Secure ingress with authenticationWhy? Only known employees and registered agents reach the platform.
    Secure egress with short-lived credentialsWhy? A leaked credential expires before an attacker can use it again.
    Secure compliance with guardrailsWhy? Guardrails stop PII leaks and unsafe output before a user sees it.
    Secure Platform with PoLPWhy? A fault or a stolen identity cannot reach data outside its own scope.
    Resiliency
    MemoryWhy? Agents continue long tasks after a failure, so employees do not repeat their work.
    ObservabilityWhy? Teams see each run, its cost, and its faults, so they make decisions from data.
    RecoveryWhy? Failed multi-step runs undo their side effects, so business data stays correct.
    Metrics
    Agentic Quality Metrics
    SRE Quality MetricsWhy? Service targets show when agents are too slow or not available for employee work.
    FinOps MetricsWhy? Cost per run and cost per user show the spend of each agent and each team.
    Vendor lock-in
    OSS StandardsWhy? Agent code uses open standards, so no single vendor controls the platform.
    Exit PathWhy? A full open-source option gives the casino a fallback if cloud prices or terms change.

    Agent registry with MLflow built-in objects: registered model, LoggedModel versions, aliases, Prompt Registry, golden sets (MLflow evaluation datasets), evaluation runs, trace assessments, no custom tables
    Agent registry concepts follow MLflow: Model Registry, Prompt Registry, Evaluation
    WIP
    Judge release loop: agents release through the MLflow registry above. Judges release as a git folder in an image.

    Numbers 1 to 5 are the same steps as in the architecture. No registry service exists. Git is the source, the image is the release, and judge.yaml is the registry entry. The Test step also writes golden-set accuracy per judge and image tag to MLflow (ns mlflow).

    judge.yaml

    id: J-T2
name: Tool use
pillar: Tools               # LLM | Memory | Tools | Environment
priority: 1                 # the orchestrator takes the top 2 per pillar
state: shadow               # shadow | active | retired. The orchestrator reads it from the image.
metrics: [ToolCorrectness, MCPUse]
when: {has_tool_calls: true}
threshold: 0.8
model: judge-small

    The other 15 configs stay on Judge Platform Options. The engine and the 3 solutions are in .
